metadata.project: store 60 gal solvent at a coating shop

summary: For a coating shop storing 60 gallons of unspecified flammable solvent, California Proposition 65 may be relevant only if the facility is in California and the solvent contains a listed chemical that causes exposures requiring a warning. The controlling statutory trigger is Health & Safety Code §25249.6 (official LegInfo source), which prohibits a business from knowingly and intentionally exposing an individual to a listed carcinogen or reproductive toxicant without first giving a clear and reasonable warning. Official LegInfo also identifies exemptions/limitations in §§25249.10 and 25249.11, including the small-business concept (persons in the course of doing business) and exposure/no-significant-risk concepts. Because the input lacks county/state, exact solvent/CAS composition, employee count, and any exposure assessment, this hypothesis is indeterminate rather than triggered or not triggered. If the site is in California, next facts needed are: whether the business has 10 or more employees, whether the solvent contains any OEHHA-listed Prop 65 chemicals, and whether storage/use can expose workers/customers/the public above applicable safe-harbor levels (NSRL/MADL) or otherwise requires a warning.
title: H-HAZMAT-PROP65: Cannot determine warning applicability without CA location, solvent identity, exposure, and employee count
